diagnostic_evidence.quote: the eigenvalues of $S_1^{-1}$, which are moved to infinity

issues.failure_explanation: The left hypothesis contains $S_2A_2$, a $q\times q$ matrix times an $m\times m$ matrix, so it is undefined. The left factor has determinant $\det S_1/\det(S_1-zI)$, so the eigenvalues it sends to infinity are those of $S_1$, not $S_1^{-1}$. Theorem th5 ($U_1R=S_1^{-1}U_1$) and the application in Section 3 ($S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1}$) need the hypothesis $U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0$. The repair must change both the hypothesis and the eigenvalue conclusion. The source offers competing readings, so this is not a single forced typo correction. No proof is given; the result is a misstated citation, so none of the three proof-based mechanisms fits.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the hypothesis as $U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0$ and state that the eigenvalues of $S_1$ are moved to infinity, consistent with th5 and Section 3.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the cited tool used for the deflation in Section 3 is undefined and points to the wrong eigenvalues for the infinity shift.
issues.title: Restated block shift-and-deflate theorem is ill-typed and inconsistent with its own shift factor and later use
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of a cited statement. The Section 3 application already uses the correct version, so no claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorems th3.2 and th5 require $S_1$ to exist and be nonsingular, and the shifted polynomial uses $(\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}-zI)^{-1}$. When $a(z)$ has roots at infinity (singular $A_2$, common for QBDs), $\Lambda_{R,1}$ has eigenvalue 0. In Example 1 ($m-\ell=1$, $\lambda_8=\infty$) one even has $\Lambda_{R,1}=0$. In such cases the construction of $\widetilde A(z)$, the factorization (eq:facat), and hence the facts that $\widetilde G,\bar G,\bar R$ solve the shifted equations are not covered by the invoked theorems. The proof of thm:added-1 starts from exactly those facts. The paper notes that $\Lambda_{G,1}$ may be singular but never addresses $\Lambda_{R,1}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the left factor as $I_m+zT_{R,1}^\top\Lambda_{R,1}(I-z\Lambda_{R,1})^{-1}T_{R,1}$. Then verify directly, for possibly singular $\Lambda_{R,1}$, the polynomiality, the coefficient formulas, the factorization (eq:facat), and that $\widetilde G,\widetilde R$ solve the shifted QMEs.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction to the $\ell\times\ell$ QMEs (eq:qmeGbar) and (eq:qmeRbar), and thus BS-CR, is unjustified whenever $A_2$ is singular, including Example 1.
issues.title: Block shift applied with $S_1=\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}$ although $\Lambda_{R,1}$ can be singular
issues.why_classification: Restricting to nonsingular $\Lambda_{R,1}$ would exclude Example 1 and typical QBDs. Avoiding that loss needs a contained new verification extending the cited theorems, not just a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $T_{R,1}\in \mathbb{R}^{(m-\ell)\times m}$ formed by the last $m-\ell$ rows of $T_R$

issues.failure_explanation: From $A_2^{(k)}=U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$, the vectors $u$ with $u^\top A_2^{(k)}$ small are the last columns of $U_2$. The rows of $T_{R,1}$ must therefore be the last rows of $U_2^\top$. Both the prose and the algorithm instead use the last rows of $U_2$, for which $T_{R,1}A_2^{(k)}\to0$ fails in general. The returned $T_{R,1}$ and $\Lambda_{R,1}$ then do not approximate the left invariant subspace of $R$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $T_R=(U_2^{(k+1)})^\top$ and partition $(U_2^{(k)})^\top$ by rows, so that the last $m-\ell$ left singular vectors are taken.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the computed $T_R$, $\Lambda_{R,1}$, $S_R$, and every quantity built from them in alg:gfull are wrong.
issues.title: Left subspace for $R$ taken from rows of $U_2^{(k)}$ instead of its left singular vectors
issues.why_classification: A local transpose correction restores the intended construction with no other changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$, each with multiplicity 2, and $\bar{G}_{11}$ is the only solution to \eqref{eq:qmeGbar} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$
with $Q$ and $Z$ unitary and $T$ and $S$ upper triangular

issues.failure_explanation: The pencil has $2\ell$ eigenvalues, each $\mu_i$ appearing twice. The graph $[I;X]$ of $\bar G_{11}$ is the deflating subspace with exactly one copy of each $\mu_i$. An arbitrary generalized Schur form may place both copies of some $\mu_i$ in the leading block. $Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1}$ is then either undefined ($Z_{11}$ singular) or a different solution with a repeated eigenvalue. The algorithm prescribes no reordering and no check that $Z_{11}$ is nonsingular.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a reordering step (e.g., ordqz) that places exactly one copy of each $\mu_i$ in $T_{11},S_{11}$, and require $Z_{11}$ nonsingular.
issues.overall_effect: The output contract of alg:QZ, and hence of alg:gfull, is not guaranteed.
issues.title: QZ step lacks the eigenvalue selection/reordering needed to pick $\bar G_{11}$
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local addition to the Higham–Kim procedure and preserves the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The $B_i$ are computed with $\bar A_{122}^{-1}$ before nonsingularity is checked. If $\bar A_{122}$ is singular, there is no alternative branch, $\bar G_{21}$ and $\bar R_{12}$ are undefined, and G_final/R_final cannot be evaluated. The assumptions of Section 2.2 do not ensure nonsingularity: $\bar A_{122}=T_{R,1}WW_{G,1}$ is a compression of the nonsingular $W$ and can be singular. Yet the output promises $G$ and $R$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add nonsingularity of $\bar A_{122}$ (equivalently of $T_{R,1}(A_1+A_2G)W_{G,1}$) as an explicit assumption and test it before forming $B_i$, or supply a separate procedure for the singular case.
issues.overall_effect: BS-CR delivers no output on part of the advertised problem class, and that part is not characterized.
issues.title: BS-CR is ill-defined when $\bar A_{122}$ is singular
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a substantive hypothesis that narrows the stated scope, or else needs a new construction, but the method otherwise survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a(z)$ has $\ell$ distinct roots $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ of modulus $1$, each with multiplicity 2

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 the values $1$ and $-1$ each appear twice. Then $G_{11}$ and $R_{11}=G_{11}^{-1}$ have each of them as a double semisimple eigenvalue. So $\det A(z)=\det(zR-I)\det P\det(zI-G)$ has roots $\pm1$ of multiplicity 4, and $\ker A(1)\supseteq\ker(I-G)$ has dimension 2. This contradicts both the claimed multiplicity 2 and the distinctness and uniqueness assumptions of Section 2.2.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ are eigenvalues of $A(z)$ of multiplicity 2.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the claim and state that Case 3 is outside the assumptions, or replace it with distinct $\mu_i$.
issues.overall_effect: Case 3 lies outside the developed theory, including uniqueness of $\bar G_{11}$ and the QZ selection, so its results do not support the claimed robustness within that theory.
issues.title: Example 3 Case 3 repeats unit-circle eigenvalues, violating the standing assumptions
issues.why_classification: Correcting the description or the test case suffices; the theory and the other cases are unaffected.
